crime: When the carts came to {WITCH_NAME}'s village, families called their children aboard house by house. No one called her name. She was left alone on the emptied road.

In the prison, one girl goes to the perimeter wall every evening, presses her palm to the stones, as near home as she can get, and records a letter to her mother on her phone. Only her little sister knows where she goes.
That little sister is {WITCH_NAME}, whose Magic makes the girl know her as family. The girl calls her "my little sister" and wraps her own shawl around her every time they meet.
One night after supper, the girl whispers to her in the dining hall: "Come to the wall tonight. Mom should hear my little sister."
That night, {WITCH_NAME} comes to the wall. The girl looks up from her recording: "Oh—sorry. I thought you were my sister." She stops recording.

Later, in the forest, the girl's face lights up when she sees {WITCH_NAME}. "There you are! I waited for you at the wall." She wraps her shawl around her little sister. {WITCH_NAME} twists it around the girl's neck until she is still, then plays back the last seconds of the recording, hears the apology that will clear her, and slips the phone back into the girl's pocket.
In the trial court, the prisoners hear that apology and conclude that whoever reached the girl that night was not her little sister, so it was not {WITCH_NAME}.
Then one prisoner replays the seconds before it. The girl's voice says, "Mom, my hand's on the stones. It's as near you as I can get."
The girl was recording at the perimeter wall, where Magic fails and no recognition holds.
Then the prisoners see it. Everywhere else, {WITCH_NAME} was the girl's little sister. At the wall she was no one, and the stranger who heard that apology was her.
fields.epitaph: The one time anyone saw her as herself, they said sorry.
execution: The execution stand raises an iron platform laid with rails, a heavy iron cart waiting at one end. She is strapped face up across the rails, ahead of the cart.
An iron bell tolls, calling iron families aboard the cart house by house. It never calls her name.
The cart rolls forward, and its full weight passes across her chest.
It rolls on, every iron face turned ahead. She lies still on the empty platform.

magic.name: One of Us
magic.text: Anyone she meets recognizes her as one of their own, someone they have always known.
